title: Flowlet diagnostics: per-packet metrics, span anchors, and privacy fences for streamed outputs
creator: Aisha K. Patel
description:
Problem: As streaming adoption grows for tool-calls, structured outputs, and long-form generation, we lack a succinct diagnostics model that ties per-output packets to distributed traces while guaranteeing that logs/telemetry do not leak PII or sensitive output. Current 'per-chunk' signals are inconsistent across clients and don't map cleanly to backend flow boundaries (prefix cache hits, KV splice, tool call fanout).

Goal: Implement a flow-level observability primitive (flowlet) that provides: (1) per-packet metrics (latency, token_count, queue_delay, kv_cache_hit), (2) stable span anchors that map flowlets to trace trees and tool-call subspans, and (3) a privacy fence mechanism that marks or redacts streamed payloads and derived telemetry according to configurable obfuscation profiles. The feature must be compatible with both existing streaming SDKs and the compatibility shim used by legacy clients.

Success criteria:
- Flowlet IDs emitted for >95% of streamed responses within runtime-1.20.
- End-to-end sample trace with flowlet -> request span -> tool-call span mapping validated in Console trace viewer.
- Telemetry store (ClickHouse/OTEL export) contains per-packet metrics with <5ms instrumentation overhead at p95.
- Privacy fence redaction applied to logs/metrics and validated by security review with no plaintext PII in retained exports.

Constraints:
- Must not change surface API for existing clients; compatibility shim should synthesize flowlets for legacy streams.
- Redaction must be reversible only for authorized audit flows using KMS-wrapped tokens.
- Work must dovetail with KV-cache boundary work and batching heuristics to avoid double-counting tokens.

Out of scope: Prompt-level content classification (will be a follow-up), fine-grained per-token semantic labels in metrics (future work).
acceptance_criteria: Flowlet ID attached to every stream emission event (server-side) and visible in console trace links
Span anchors correlate flowlet IDs to root request span and tool-call spans in distributed traces
Per-packet metrics emitted to telemetry layer: packet_latency_ms, packet_token_count, queue_delay_ms, kv_cache_hit_bool
Privacy fence flags applied to emitted events; redacted exports strip payloads and replace with deterministic placeholders
Compatibility shim available in SDKs to synthesize flowlets for legacy stream formats
Performance regression <5ms p95 added latency; storage cost increase <8% for telemetry pipeline
work_log: 2026-02-18 - Ticket created by Aisha. Initial problem statement and goals. Linked to streaming observability epic ENG-32001.

2026-02-23 - Investigation: Miguel ran a synthetic harness showing current per-chunk telemetry misses when KV cache is hit during initial prefix. Recorded sample traces: https://redwood.internal/traces/flowlet-synth-2026-02-23
2026-02-27 - Design sync with Observability and Security. Decided on flowlet as a short-lived opaque ID (UUID v4) plus an anchor offset for mapping into request spans.
2026-03-03 - Prototype: server emits 'flowlet.start' and 'flowlet.packet' events in stream envelope. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8746
2026-03-05 - Security review kickoff: identified need for 'privacy fence' metadata that signals redaction level (none, soft, hard) and KMS-scoped audit token generation.

2026-03-08 - Observability agreed on metric names and Telemetry schema. Created ClickHouse ingestion mapping and OTLP exporter config. Dashboard mock: https://grafana.redwood/streaming/flowlet-metrics

2026-03-10 - Integration test failed: legacy client streams without envelope caused missing flowlet IDs. Follow-up: compatibility shim design to synthesize flowlet.start on stream open in proxy layer.
notes: Implementation idea: attach flowlet_id and packet_index to stream envelope; packet_index resets after canary rollouts to avoid long-lived counters.
Span anchoring: include (flowlet_id, anchor_offset_ms) as span attributes; router will emit link span pointing to root request span using trace_id/parent_id mapping.
Privacy fence: three-tier model - 'none' (full payload), 'soft' (hash+schema only), 'hard' (no payload, placeholder). Redaction configured per-customer and per-route.

Compatibility shim: proxy inspects first bytes; if stream is legacy newline-delimited text, synthesize flowlet.start with best-effort token_count estimate and emit flowlet.packet for subsequent chunks.
Telemetry retention: consider compressed packet aggregates for long tails to control cost. Store raw packet telemetry for 7 days, aggregates for 90 days.
risks: False negatives: synthesized flowlets might mismatch actual server boundaries causing trace mismatches
Performance: extra attributes and envelope wrapping could increase serialization cost; need microbenchmarks across GPU hosts
Security: misconfiguration of privacy fence could leak content in logs if not applied consistently across exporters
next_steps: Complete prototype PR feedback and land minimal 'flowlet.start' + 'flowlet.packet' events (runtime change)
Ship SDK compatibility shim in node/python SDKs to synthesize envelopes for legacy clients
Add telemetry ingestion mapping and Grafana panels to staging cluster
Complete security review and add automated redaction tests in CI
